title: Members of the six-piece recording band
summary: He names the sidemen, notes there was no bass or trombone, and explains the doubling that made it sound larger.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I don't remember now before, when you mentioned your band in New York, if you told everybody that was in it, how many pieces was that band that made the records?
We only had six pieces of band. Six? Yeah. There wasn't more than that. No, it was six. We only had the drum, piano.

It was Ward Crosby. He was a drummer. We used to call him Bucket, a little short fella. He lives in Chicago. That's his home. And we had Eugene Ware, Eugene Porter, and I had Alfred Gishard, and Walter Williams. He had no bass. No bass. No trombone. Just six pieces. I don't know. A whole lot of people thought it was more than six pieces for one reason. You see now, the trumpet player, I mean the tenor-psychopone player used to double on trumpet. See he could play trumpet too.
Oh so that's what he did then.
Yeah, then he played clarinet too. You see, so a lot of people thought that we had more than six, but that's all we had. We didn't have no bass at all.
Were they all made one afternoon, one day, or whenever it was?
